prerequisites: Ability to read and understand documentation written in English

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to build, exploit and manage telecommunication networks, services, processes and applications, understood as systems for capturing, transporting, representing, processing, storing, managing and presenting multimedia information, from the point of view of telematic services.
Ability to build, exploit and manage telematic services using analytical tools for planning, sizing and analysis.
Ability to follow the technological progress of transmission, switching and processing to improve telematic networks and services.
Know and apply technological advances in communication infrastructures and telematic services, applying quality criteria and service level agreements.
Develop design, implementation, management and improvement processes for communication networks and telematic services based on Deming's continuous improvement cycle.
Design and apply methods of collaboration with clients and service personnel responsible for managing it with quality throughout its entire life cycle.
Design strategies for placing communication services on the market taking into account technological, cost and quality parameters.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Service Management and ITIL v3
Elaboration of BPMN diagrams for ITSM process modeling
Attitude, conduct, and culture in IT Management
Simulation of ITSM processes with the Apollo 13 case study
teaching_methods: Laboratory / field / computer lab / language lab practices
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required in the Partial Exam, Final Exam, Group Work, and Team Simulation, along with 80% attendance to laboratory practice sessions. The final grade is calculated as 0.1 * EP + 0.4 * EF + 0.4 * TG + 0.1 * SE, and must be 5 or higher to pass. If minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated result and 4.5. For extraordinary calls, only the Group Work grade from the ordinary call is retained. A global theory exam (ET) must be passed with at least 5 out of 10 points, and the final grade is 0.5 * ET + 0.5 * TG. For differentiated evaluation, a global theory exam (ET) and individual work (TI) must each be passed with at least 5 out of 10 points, and the final grade is 0.5 * ET + 0.5 * TI.
